info.bio:
El estadounidense Matthew Sweet es una de las figuras esenciales del pop de guitarras de los últimos 15 años. Mentar su nombre es provocar la admiración entre los amantes del powerpop.
La carrera de Matthew Sweet presenta una singular animadversión hacia el éxito. O hacia la presión que éste conlleva. Cada paso hacia la popularidad que ha dado, y su currículo presenta un par de discos de oro, ha estado seguido de un oscurecimiento de su sonido, cuando no de una reclusión en sí mismo.

scenes.name: Cantautores de los ochenta
scenes.author: Piero Scaruffi
scenes.desc: Absorbida la new wave, el mundo de los cantautores no vuelve a ser el mismo: los referentes pasan a ser Dylan, Neil Young, Cohen, Tim Buckley y Joni Mitchell. Las mujeres recuperan su estatus de seres filosóficos: Phranc, Suzanne Vega, Tracy Chapman, Melissa Etheridge, Michelle Shocked, Barbara Manning, Lucinda y Victoria Williams, Indigo Girls y, en Canadá, Jane Siberry, Mary Margaret O'Hara y Sarah McLachlan. Excéntricos: Jandek, Daniel Johnston, David Thomas, Alejandro Escovedo; en California, Stan Ridgway, Chris Isaak y Smog. En Gran Bretaña, Billy Bragg, Robyn Hitchcock, Julian Cope y, la voz más importante de la década, Nick Cave, predicador del apocalipsis moral (From Her To Eternity, The Good Son). Sinéad O'Connor, Sting, Morrissey, Momus; el pop celta de Enya y Loreena McKennitt; al cambiar la década, Joe Henry, Daniel Lanois y Bob Mould.

podcast.title: Career Trajectory and Influences
podcast.body: Originally from Nebraska, Matthew Sweet relocated to Athens, Georgia, where he was involved in a band with Michael Stipe's sister. His career took some time to gain momentum, but it found its footing with his third album, "Girlfriend," in 1991. He exemplified the "Beatlesque" approach of 90s alt-rock, paying close attention to pre-Sgt. Pepper influences. "Matthew Sweet, a dude originally from Nebraska who ended up in Athens, Georgia in a band with Michael Steibes' sister."

xref.title: Another Roadside Attraction Festival (1993)
xref.body: The Tragically Hip organized the festival "Another Roadside Attraction" in 1993, 1995, and 1997. This festival was one of several Canadian-based summer music events during the 90s, showcasing the growing strength and popularity of domestic music. "There was another roadside attraction, which was organized by the Trajically Hip in 1993, 1995 and 1997."

xref.title: Later Career Work with Frank Black and Matthew Sweet
xref.body: Demonstrating her enduring career, Carol K played on Frank Black of the Pixies' 2006 record "Fast Man Raider." She also collaborated with Matthew Sweet in 1999, appearing on his album "In Reverse" on the song "Faith in You," further solidifying her legacy as an important figure in rock history. "She even played with Frank Black of the Pixies on a 2006 record called Fast Man Raider."
